input.text: 2025 review: Daniel's 2025 backdoor Roth conversion. Daniel contributed $7,000.00 nondeductible to traditional IRA SYN-15870003 on 2025-02-11 and converted $7,000.00 to Roth IRA SYN-15870004 on 2025-02-14. There were no earnings and the IRA fee was $0.00. Form 8606 (Daniel): line 1 $7,000 nondeductible contribution; line 2 $0 prior basis (tax profile, basis at 2024-12-31); line 3 $7,000; line 6 $0 value of all traditional/SEP/SIMPLE IRAs at 2025-12-31 (SYN-15870003 closed the year at $0.00 cash, no positions); line 8 $7,000 converted; lines 9-11 $7,000, ratio 1.000, $7,000 nontaxable; line 13 $7,000; line 14 $0 basis carried to 2026; line 18 $0 taxable. Result: none of the conversion is taxable income for 2025. The pro-rata rule does not bite, because the 401(k) SYN-15870002 (about $178k at 2025-12-31) is an employer plan and is not counted on line 6. The 2025 Form 1099-R for SYN-15870003 shows box 1 $7,000, box 2a $7,000 with box 2b (taxable amount not determined) checked, and code 2. Box 2a is not the taxable amount; Form 8606 sets it at $0. Decided: the firm does not prepare returns, so we will send these figures to Sofia and Daniel for their preparer, with the reminder to file Form 8606 (Parts I and II) with the 2025 joint return or extension. Caveat: this assumes Daniel held no traditional, SEP or SIMPLE IRA anywhere else at 2025-12-31; to be confirmed with him. Going forward, rolling the 401(k) into an IRA would bring pre-tax money into the pro-rata calculation for any year with a backdoor conversion.

content.text:
**Answer: none of Daniel's 2025 backdoor Roth conversion is taxable income. The taxable amount is $0, and the basis carried to 2026 is $0.**

**Why**
- **Contribution and conversion:** Daniel put $7,000 nondeductible into traditional IRA SYN-15870003 on 11 Feb 2025. On 14 Feb he converted exactly $7,000 to Roth IRA SYN-15870004. The money earned nothing in between and the IRA was charged no fees.
- **Basis:** He had no basis from earlier years ($0 at 31 Dec 2024, per the tax profile). So his 2025 basis is the $7,000 contribution.
- **Pro-rata rule:** The rule looks at the value of all of Daniel's traditional, SEP and SIMPLE IRAs on 31 Dec 2025. That figure is $0, because SYN-15870003 was empty at year-end.
